subject: how to make plots from different data frames

messages.author: 56aba7f8b1fa173f
messages.subject: how to make plots from different data frames
parts:
I want to make one plot via combining  two data frames. But, I got the error message as below:
After research some solution, I still pinpoint this question.

Error in extract.coef.default(model) : 
  'names' attribute [2] must be the same length as the vector [0]

And, this is my code as below:

library(ggplot2)
dt <- read.table("/R/10G.csv", header=TRUE, sep="\t", na.strings="NA", dec=".", strip.white=TRUE)
da <- read.table("/R/20G.csv", header=TRUE, sep="\t", na.strings="NA", dec=".", strip.white=TRUE)

library(plyr)
dd.mean <- ddply(dt, 'Thread', summarize, TPS = round(mean(TPS), 2), RT = round(mean(RT), 2))
da.mean <- ddply(dt, 'Thread', summarize, TPS = round(mean(TPS), 2), RT = round(mean(RT), 2))

p1 <- ggplot(dd.mean, aes(x = Thread, y = RT)) + 
  labs(size = 1, x='Threads', y='Responese Time') +
  geom_line(size = 1, alpha = 0.3, colour = "red", stat="identity") + 
  geom_point(size = 3, alpha = 1, colour = "red", stat="identity") +  
  geom_text(size = 3, x = dd.mean$Thread, label = dd.mean$RT, vjust = 1.5) +  
  scale_x_continuous(breaks=dd.mean$Thread, labels=factor(dd.mean$Thread)) +
  scale_y_continuous(breaks = round(seq(min(dd.mean$RT), max(dd.mean$RT), by = 100),1)) +
  geom_text(size = 3, x = dd.mean$Thread, label = dd.mean$RT, vjust = 1.5) 

p2 <- ggplot(da.mean, aes(x = Thread, y = RT)) + 
  labs(size = 1, x='Threads', y='Responese Time') +
  geom_line(size = 1, alpha = 0.3, colour = "red", stat="identity") + 
  geom_point(size = 3, alpha = 1, colour = "red", stat="identity") +  
  geom_text(size = 3, x = da.mean$Thread, label = da.mean$RT, vjust = 1.5)  
  
library(coefplot)
multiplot(p1,p2)

messages.author: bfc2eb6b71169017
messages.subject: Re: how to make plots from different data frames
parts:
From what I read about `multiplot` from `coefplot` package, the function's made for plotting model coefficients, while you're trying to plot two ggplot figures. I'm assuming you're trying to "arrange" a bunch of figures into a larger figure. If that's the case, try

library(gridExtra)
grid.arrange()

See also http://stackoverflow.com/questions/6681145/how-can-i-arrange-an-arbitrary-number-of-ggplots-using-grid-arrange

Cheers,
Roman
